title: I house sat for a couple who left forty rules on the fridge. I broke rule twenty before dinner.
story:
The rules were typed and numbered. Water the ferns. Feed the fish. Rule twenty said, If the grandfather clock chimes thirteen, do not count it twice.

I thought it was a joke. The clock was beautiful and old, and at midnight on my first night it chimed twelve. I relaxed.

At 1 AM it chimed thirteen.

I counted, because anyone would. Thirteen. Then the clock chimed again, and I counted again without meaning to.

The house felt different afterward. The ferns had turned toward me. The fish tank was dark, and all the fish hung at the glass, staring into the room.

From upstairs a door opened. Footsteps crossed the ceiling, then stopped above my head. Rule twenty-one was printed under the magnet. It said, Whatever you counted twice will now be counted.

I heard knocking. Once. Twice. Then slowly, on the floor right beneath my feet, where there is no room, only foundation.

I stopped breathing and listened to it count, slow and patient, getting closer to the top.

It reached me.

It had my number.
premise: house sitting rule about the clock chiming thirteen; counting twice summons something that counts you
